items.headline: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 custom AI chip, with large-scale deployment from 2027
items.why: Another hyperscaler moving inference onto its own silicon (company-claimed ~40% more output per unit of power than leading GPU systems) caps the share of its AI spend that goes to Nvidia over time.

sources.title: GeekWire: Microsoft makes 'biggest bet yet' on its own silicon

items.headline: ASML posts record Q3 revenue of EUR 11.7B and guides Q4 to EUR 14.2-15.2B
items.why: The chip-equipment maker's guide implies customers are still expanding capacity sharply, which is the demand signal the AI buildout trade depends on.

sources.title: Tech Startups: Top Tech News Today, October 14, 2026

items.headline: CoreWeave falls about 25% on the week as AI financing worries spread to credit
items.why: Corporate spreads widened and the company's high-yield debt traded near 14-15%, showing the AI buildout's funding cost is now a market risk rather than a footnote.

items.headline: Japan to invest up to $21B in two GlobalFoundries New York fabs; US stake rises to about 7%
items.why: Allied state-backed money is now funding US chip capacity directly, shifting where leading and mature-node supply gets built.

items.headline: Bitcoin pinned near $82K with US spot ETF flows at roughly zero
items.why: Without fund buying, price has failed repeatedly at $83-84K, so the range holds until flows return or something else forces a break.

sources.title: CryptoTicker: Bitcoin at $81,963, ETF inflows close to zero

items.headline: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs lose about $1.15B combined over Oct 7-12
items.why: Institutional demand turned net negative for the month ahead of hot inflation data, removing the main marginal buyer.

items.headline: September CPI hit 3.7% and PPI 6.3% year over year, both above expectations
items.why: Hotter inflation keeps the Fed biased toward hiking, with futures near 89% for a December increase.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield spiked to 5.33% after CPI, then settled near 5.09%
items.why: A 10-year above 5% raises the discount rate on every long-duration asset, which is why tech took the brunt of the week's selling.

items.headline: Missile aimed at Saudi Red Sea export port Yanbu intercepted as Hormuz shipping stays disrupted
items.why: Yanbu is the route that bypasses Hormuz, so threats there remove the main workaround for Gulf crude and are driving the oil move.

sources.title: EnergyNow: Oil surges as Middle East supply fears push Brent near $110

items.headline: Brent settles at $109.86 (touched $110, highest since May); WTI at $101.41, up 10.4% on the week
items.why: Oil above $100 feeds straight into the inflation prints and rate-hike odds above, even with 20M+ barrels of emergency IEA releases and a US reserve exchange offsetting part of it.

sources.title: EnergyNow: Oil surges as Middle East supply fears push Brent near $110

items.headline: US crude inventories fall 8.6M barrels to 415.6M, far more than expected
items.why: A large draw while Russian refining is being hit by strikes tightens the near-term balance and supports the price floor.

sources.title: EnergyNow: Oil surges as Middle East supply fears push Brent near $110

items.headline: Gold holds near $4,190 even as the dollar sits near a one-and-a-half-year high
items.why: Gold absorbing a strong dollar and higher yield expectations means safe-haven demand is offsetting the usual headwinds.

items.headline: Nasdaq Composite closes at 26,140, down 4.5% on the week and ending a four-week winning streak
items.why: The index gave back the gains from its run to a record close near 27,244 earlier in the month, so that level is now overhead resistance.

items.headline: S&P 500 ends near 7,659, down about 2% on the week; Dow up 0.7% for a second weekly gain
items.why: Leadership rotated away from AI-linked tech, with the semiconductor ETF down about 8% through Thursday and a further 4% Friday, while the less tech-heavy Dow held up.

items.headline: Bitcoin range: support at $80K, resistance in the $83-84K area
items.why: Price dipped under $81K on Oct 13 and recovered, so $80K is the level whose loss would mark a break of the October range.
